status: nominal catalogue values, NOT enclosures; every decimal below is an exact rational input of the model

source.fit: Rosenthal et al. 2021, ApJS 255, 8 (California Legacy Survey I), doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abe23c
source.retrieved_from: NASA Exoplanet Archive, Planetary Systems table (ps), rows with pl_refname = ROSENTHAL_ET_AL__2021 for hostname 'HD 11964', TAP sync query on 2026-11-01
source.cross_check: docs/explorations/amd-crossing/A7-practical.md section 5 (periods 37.9196, 1935.0 d; m sin i 24.3, 201 Earth masses; e .106, .101; a .2315, 3.185 AU) agree to the digits shown there

msun_over_mearth.source: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 nominal GM_sun / GM_earth (the LP-QUANT convention, scripts/lp_quant/systems.py)

mass_msun.source: archive st_mass of the Rosenthal et al. 2021 rows

omega_star_deg.note: argument of periastron of the STELLAR reflex orbit (RV convention); the planet's is omega + 180 deg

model.name: planar Newtonian three-body problem (star + HD 11964 c + HD 11964 b), LP normalization
model.hamiltonian: KAM.Planetary.movingHamiltonian 1 1 nu mu (frozen), heliocentric positions, rescaled barycentric momenta, G = 1, star mass 1
model.masses: planet masses = m sin i (edge-on, coplanar orbits assumed: sin i = 1, zero mutual inclination); m_i / M_star = mu * nu_i, mu = largest ratio
model.length_unit: AU (the axes below follow from the periods by Kepler's third law with G M_star = 1)
model.time_unit: sqrt(AU^3 / (G M_star)) = 1 yr / (2 pi sqrt(M_star / M_sun)) with G M_sun = 4 pi^2 AU^3 / yr^2 (Gaussian convention)
model.axes: a_i = (M_star * (P_i / days_per_year)^2)^(1/3) AU, read as the LP canonical axis a_i = (Lambda_i / nu_i)^2 of the nominal state
model.phases: mean anomaly at the epoch from tc (radvel convention: true anomaly f = pi/2 - omega_star at tc); planet periastron omega_p = omega_star + pi; common node, so varpi_i = omega_p,i in the orbital plane
